purpose: Design for document search: pre-search freshness checks, the search result contract with the search AI, and resolution of DLIDs to recorded paths via resolve-dlid.
summary: Pre-search check distinguishes rebuild-not-needed, rebuild-needed, and undeterminable, and the user chooses between rebuild-then-search and searching the existing version
Undeterminable results are treated as failures: search stops and the cause is returned, never falling back silently to an old version
Rebuild scale shown to the user is counted by script from the comparison (new, departed, moved, changed, no-ID, duplicate-ID, AI-generation needed)
Each search candidate carries document ID, recorded path, reason, optional section, ToC key, version, and freshness
Read-only search AI reads every entry of a ToC copy and favors recall over precision when choosing candidates
ToC copy contains document info and section IDs with headings, but no paths, content hashes, references, or check results
resolve-dlid resolves each DLID from recorded state and the file at the recorded path, verifying frontmatter doc_link_id or heading-end section DLID
Unresolved DLIDs return recorded path not found or no record, without exploring other locations or asserting the path as current
Resolved results include recorded content hash; the ToC, state, and target documents are never written to
tasks: Designing or implementing the query-docs search flow
Implementing the pre-search freshness check script
Implementing or modifying the resolve-dlid script
Writing the query-worker search AI instructions
Reviewing search result format and freshness reporting
Deciding handling of stale or undeterminable ToC during search
Writing tests for search and DLID resolution
